name: Wolves at the Door: Garou Crossover Rules

pages.name: Wolves at the Door: Garou Crossover Rules

text.content:
Vampires and werewolves (Garou to themselves, Lupines to Kindred) are ancient, embittered enemies — Garou believe Kindred are the Wyrm's handiwork made flesh. Despite that, the two sometimes work together in secret against common enemies. Gangrel are the Kindred most likely to deal with Garou and their Kinfolk peaceably, with Nosferatu a distant second where Bone Gnawers are concerned; urban Kindred are most likely to run into Bone Gnawer or Glass Walker Kinfolk, and might find relatively less hostile ground with Children of Gaia, Stargazers, or Uktena. All bets are off with every other tribe, and no Kindred should ever crash a Garou moot — Earth Meld barely helps against twenty nine-foot killing machines.

Wyrm-Taint and Detection

Kindred and ghouls with three or fewer Humanity Traits smell of the Wyrm to a Garou using Wyrm-taint detection. Vampires following a Path of Enlightenment automatically read as Wyrm-tainted regardless of rating — except Path of the Feral Heart, which reads like Humanity for this purpose.

Drinking Lupine Blood

A vampire who drinks werewolf vitae finds each Blood Trait counts double, but suffers the Negative Mental Trait Impatient until the blood is spent (should be roleplayed as barely-restrained frenzy tension) and adds one Trait to the difficulty of any frenzy test until it's used. Blood is spent in the order it was taken (last in, first out).

Vampires who specifically hunt werewolves for their blood aren't wrong to: the true (and little-known) mechanism is tied to the werewolf's Pure Breed Background. On the turn after a Kindred spends a Blood Trait taken from a werewolf with Pure Breed, she gains extra actions and Strength-related Trait bonuses scaled to that Pure Breed rating (as a supplement to, but not stacking beyond, existing Celerity/Potence effects). If Blood Traits from werewolves of different Pure Breed ratings are spent in the same turn, only the first one spent has an effect, and any Garou-blood bonus lasts only for the turn immediately following expenditure.

Garou Drinking Cainite Blood

A Garou who drinks vampire vitae can be ghouled (gaining one level of Potence like any other ghoul) or even blood bound, though few Garou will hold Cainite blood down voluntarily — most would rather vomit it back up. A Garou who drinks or is forced to drink Cainite vitae becomes Wyrm-tainted; a Rite of Cleansing is normally sufficient to remove both the blood and the taint.

Banes

In the Umbra, spirits touched by the Wyrm are called Banes by the Garou. Banes are normally unable to possess Kindred (attempts leave the Bane trapped instead), but Kindred who indulge their Beast through violence, bloodshed, or corruption attract Banes as spiritual scavengers waiting on the fallout.

Discipline / Gift Interactions

  • Animalism: Feral Whispers does not grant understanding of the Garou tongue (communication as wolves still works). No animal-targeting power affects a Garou or other Changing Breed, including in Lupus or animal breed forms. Garou do have Beasts (expressed via Rage) and can be affected by Beast-targeting powers.
  • Celerity: Garou can spend Rage for extra actions to match a Kindred's Celerity-driven extra actions.
  • Dementation: Voice of Madness forces a targeted Lupine to test for fox frenzy, testing Willpower against Rage.
  • Obfuscate: Works normally against Garou. Enhanced-senses Gifts can attempt to pierce it the way Auspex does, substituting the Garou's Rank for the Auspex rating in the challenge.
  • Protean: A Kindred using Shape of the Beast to become a wolf cannot understand the Garou tongue and won't smell fully right to Garou senses.

Garou Gifts vs. Kindred

  • Healing Gifts (e.g. Mother's Touch): Only work on living creatures; a vampire is not living and cannot be healed by them (nor by Gifts that mend only inanimate objects).
  • Heightened Senses: Can be used to pierce Chimerstry or Obfuscate; adjudicate using the core "Case Law"/"Relative Power Level" crossover guidance.
  • Resist Toxin: Doesn't prevent a Garou from being ghouled or bound, but does allow a soak attempt against Quietus, Thanatosis, and other Disciplines that work via blood contact, disease, or decay.
  • Scent of Running Water: Can be pierced by a vampire tracking by scent using Auspex, using the Auspex-vs-Obfuscate challenge mechanic with the Garou's Rank standing in for the Discipline rating.
  • Scent of the True Form: On a win only (not a tie), lets a Garou detect a Kindred who is using Possession or Subsume the Spirit on a mortal or animal vessel.
  • Sense Magic: Detects Thaumaturgy and Dark Thaumaturgy in use, but not other Cainite Disciplines.

vtmlarp.source: Storytellers Guide, "Those Who Hunt the Night" - Wolves at the Door
